newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Druze soldiers say Israeli discos discriminate.
newsitem.headline: Druze soldiers say Israeli discos discriminate.

text.p: Arab Druze soldiers in the Israeli army complained on Wednesday that northern communities who counted on them to provide security had discriminated against them at nightclubs.
"When we get to the kibbutz or community...sometimes when they hear we're speaking Arabic they prevent us from entering the place," one of the Druze told Israel Radio.
The Druze -- a secretive offshoot of Islam -- are the only non-Jewish minority who must serve in Israel's army. Israel's Druze, numbering more than 60,000, speak both Hebrew and Arabic.
"I will deal with this so that it is resolved immediately," Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai told a group of Druze soldiers on a visit to Israel's northern front.

Pub operators insisted they had not discriminated but barred people known to have been involved previously in violence. One said a rule at his pub allowing entry only to couples was aimed at curbing friction.

"We wouldn't be surprised if whoever is behind this false report were certain people who in the past were involved in violent acts at our pub. Some of them were Druze and some of them were Jews," pub manager Barak Shahar told Israel Radio.

"If there is improper behaviour on the part of civilian elements, we will deal with it so that everywhere you will be received with the honour appropriate and in the manner suitable for receiving Israeli army fighters," he told the soldiers.
